I will keep my farm simple and stable this year. I only have 4.1 mu, and some people in my family work off-farm, so I do not want a management plan that needs too much labor or too much risk. Because I have well irrigation, I will rely on the wheat-maize system on most of my land since it fits my experience and gives me steady grain output across the year. I will put 3.1 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. I will keep 1.0 mu for cotton because I already grow it, it spreads my risk, and I can manage it with irrigation, but I will not expand it because cotton needs more spraying and more field attention. For seed, I will use improved or hybrid seed where it matters for yield and stability. For fertilizer, I will stay in a moderate range instead of pushing for the highest possible input level, because my land is small and I want dependable returns rather than chasing maximum yield. I will irrigate wheat more than maize, and I will spray cotton more than the grains because that is where pest pressure usually costs me more. For tillage, I will use rotary tillage for wheat and cotton, and I will use no-tillage maize after wheat to save time and hold moisture.
